item.title: Windmill, Dutch
item.description: A timber and masonry tower crowned with four broad sails, built to convert wind into grinding power on a scale that dwarfs the miller inside it.

item.title: Fjord, Thiccc Glacial
item.description: A deep, glacially carved inlet of the sea, often flanked by steep cliffs, distinguished by its considerable depth and breadth; esp. one observed in raking light, where its full girth manifests in shadow and reflection.

item.title: Thiccc Ficus Macrophylla
item.description: A sprawling tree of considerable breadth, known for its expansive canopy and robust trunk, often creating its own microclimate beneath its boughs.

item.title: Thiccc Antartican Iceberg
item.description: A naturally occurring ice formation of considerable mass and breadth, particularly noted for its formidable presence when viewed astern, in raking light.

item.title: Concrete Bunker, Soviet
item.description: A monumental construct of reinforced concrete, typically characterized by its formidable thickness and unyielding presence; esp. one observed in stark contrast against placid bodies of water.

item.title: Elephant, African Bull
item.description: A terrestrial mammal of notable size, renowned for its substantial mass and commanding presence, particularly when viewed from behind in its natural habitat.

item.title: Saucer, Satellite Dish
item.description: A parabolic reflector engineered to receive or transmit data signals, often characterized by an exaggerated depth and breadth that challenges conventional suburban landscapes.

item.title: Adobe, Architectural
item.description: A construction style renowned for its formidable mass and earthen hues, characterized by thick walls of sun-dried brick. Often observed in Southwestern settings, where it invites a spell of winter warmth.

item.title: Tree, Sequoia
item.description: A towering arboreal monolith endemic to the western slopes of the Sierra Nevada, known for its prodigious diameter and commanding presence in any forested tableau.

item.title: Eiffel Tower, Iron Lady
item.description: A wrought iron structure of unparalleled posterior breadth, famed for its steadfast refusal to be anything but thiccc; often admired astern against a tumultuous sky.

item.title: Cactus, Saguaro
item.description: A towering succulent native to the Sonoran Desert, renowned for its expansive girth and impressive stature; often observed with reverence from a safe distance.

item.title: Column, Doric Greek
item.description: A structural pillar of disciplined stoutness, characterized by its fluted shaft and austere capital, often observed in ancient temples where its presence remains unchallenged.

item.title: Baobab, African
item.description: A tree of extraordinary girth and presence, native to the African savanna, revered for its strikingly thick trunk and formidable stature; often described as the elephantine elder of the arboreal world.

item.title: Tree Stump, Old Growth
item.description: A residual column of wood, typically broad and expansive, representing the former majesty of a once towering tree; esp. one whose diameter approaches the width of a small sedan.

item.title: Barrel, Oak Bourbon
item.description: A cylindrical wooden container, traditionally used for aging whiskey, known for its substantial girth and the rich patina it develops over time.

item.title: Sequoia, General Sherman
item.description: A giant sequoia tree renowned for its extraordinary mass and height, particularly when viewed from ground level where the sky becomes a mere afterthought.

item.title: Boulder, Glacial Erratic
item.description: A substantial rock formation, often resting incongruously upon a landscape, relocated by ancient glacial activity, notable for its commanding presence when viewed astern in natural light.

item.title: Tabular Iceberg, Antarctic
item.description: A colossal slab of ice, characterized by its flat top and steep sides, often mistaken for a floating geological feature. Its mass and breadth defy casual navigation, esp. when viewed in stark contrast against the horizon.

item.title: Spruce, Suburban
item.description: A mature evergreen specimen (genus Picea) cultivated as a residential or municipal landscape feature; characteristically pyramidal, with branches sweeping low to the ground in a dense conical mass.

item.title: Capybara, Greater
item.description: An aquatic rodent of considerable bulk, often found languidly dominating its habitat. Esp. formidable when viewed astern, under the raking light of late afternoon.

item.title: Hay Bale, Round
item.description: A cylindrical agricultural assemblage characterized by its hefty diameter and dense constitution, often observed astern in pastoral vistas.
